description: Turning raw sequencing reads into biological answers: sequencing technologies and their error profiles, read quality control, mapping to a reference, de novo genome assembly, variant calling and annotation, RNA-seq gene expression analysis, and pathogen genomics for outbreak surveillance. Practised as complete analysis pipelines run on small public datasets with browser-based tools, working through cases such as Vibrio cholerae and Lassa virus genomes and human variants shaped by malaria.
modelledOn: Compeau and Pevzner, Bioinformatics Algorithms: An Active Learning Approach
WHO, Global Genomic Surveillance Strategy for Pathogens with Pandemic and Epidemic Potential
outcomes: Compare short-read and long-read sequencing technologies and choose a platform, read length and depth suited to a genomic question.
Assess and clean raw reads using quality scores, adapter trimming and duplication metrics, and justify each filtering decision.
Map reads to a reference genome with indexed aligners and interpret SAM and BAM records, mapping quality and coverage.
Assemble a genome from reads with de Bruijn and overlap graph methods and evaluate the assembly with contiguity and completeness measures.
Call, filter and annotate genetic variants and analyse differential gene expression from RNA-seq counts with appropriate statistics.
Apply pathogen genomics to outbreak surveillance, from sample to lineage assignment and resistance prediction, and report the findings to public health teams.

units.title: Genomes and sequencing technologies
topics: Genome organisation in bacteria, viruses and eukaryotes: genes, repeats, plasmids, ploidy; the human reference genome
Sanger sequencing and the move to massively parallel sequencing; cost and throughput
Illumina sequencing by synthesis: library preparation, cluster amplification, single-end and paired-end reads
Long-read technologies: nanopore sequencing (MinION) and PacBio HiFi; error profiles and when long reads are essential
Experimental design: coverage and depth (Lander-Waterman), multiplexing and barcodes, whole-genome versus exome versus amplicon
Portable sequencing for field surveillance: nanopore runs in national and regional laboratories in Africa

units.title: Read quality control
topics: FASTQ in depth: Phred scores, encodings, per-base and per-read quality
Quality reports with FastQC and MultiQC: base composition, GC distribution, overrepresented sequences, duplication
Adapter and quality trimming; length filtering; removing host and contaminant reads
Quality control for nanopore reads: read length distributions and basecalling accuracy
Recording QC decisions so an analysis can be reproduced

units.title: Read mapping
topics: Why mapping differs from classical alignment: speed, seeds and the scale of the problem
Indexing a reference: suffix arrays, the Burrows-Wheeler transform and the FM-index; backward search
Short-read aligners (BWA, Bowtie2) and long-read aligners (minimap2); paired-end constraints
SAM and BAM formats: flags, CIGAR strings, mapping quality; sorting, indexing and viewing with samtools
Coverage, insert size and duplicate marking; inspecting alignments in a genome browser

units.title: Genome assembly
topics: The assembly problem: reads, overlaps, contigs and scaffolds; why repeats make it hard
Overlap-layout-consensus and string graphs for long reads
De Bruijn graphs from k-mers: Eulerian paths, choice of k, error correction, bubbles and tips
Assemblers in practice: SPAdes for bacteria, Flye for long reads; hybrid assembly
Evaluating assemblies: N50, misassemblies, BUSCO completeness, comparison with a reference
Genome annotation basics: gene prediction and functional labelling of a bacterial assembly

units.title: Variant calling
topics: Types of variation: SNVs, indels, structural variants, copy-number variation
Genotype likelihoods and Bayesian variant calling; how base and mapping quality enter the model
Calling pipelines: GATK best practices and bcftools; base quality recalibration and joint genotyping
The VCF format; hard filtering versus model-based filtering; transition/transversion ratio as a sanity check
Variant annotation and effect prediction; population databases such as gnomAD and the under-representation of African genomes
Case study: the HbS allele, G6PD deficiency and other human variants shaped by malaria selection

units.title: Gene expression analysis
topics: RNA-seq experimental design: replicates, depth, batch effects, stranded and poly-A libraries
Spliced alignment and pseudo-alignment for quantification (HISAT2, Salmon); counts per gene
Normalisation: library size, TPM, size factors; exploratory analysis with PCA and clustering
Differential expression with negative binomial models (DESeq2, edgeR); multiple testing and the false discovery rate
Interpreting results: volcano plots, gene set and pathway enrichment
Single-cell RNA-seq in brief

units.title: Pathogen genomics for disease surveillance
topics: From sample to sequence in an outbreak: amplicon schemes, turnaround time and laboratory networks
Lineage and genotype assignment for SARS-CoV-2, Vibrio cholerae and Lassa virus; typing schemes such as MLST
Antimicrobial resistance prediction from genomes; resistance gene databases
Linking genomes to case data; sharing sequences through public archives and GISAID
Case study: genomic surveillance of cholera and Lassa fever in West Africa and the Africa CDC Pathogen Genomics Initiative

units.title: Reproducible pipelines and project
topics: Workflow managers (Snakemake, Nextflow) and containers for reproducible pipelines
Compute, storage and cost on limited infrastructure; working with shared servers and the cloud
Ethics and governance of genomic data: consent, community engagement, benefit sharing, data sovereignty in Africa
Project: an end-to-end analysis of a public bacterial or viral outbreak dataset with a surveillance report
